title: RO-MT085-RoleManagerGui

scope.summary:
GOAL: Deliver the operator-facing Role Manager: (a) a native egui Role Manager pane in handshake_native for the full role lifecycle — list / create / edit (new version) / version history / retire / approve-draft — and (b) a role picker integrated into the operator_chat_pane launch flow so every session launch can carry a role; plus (c) a READ-ONLY React surface in the swarm launch UI (list/pick over IPC). Roles are operator-authored/approved and model-consumed: this pane is where drafts (operator-authored or MT-084 imports) get reviewed and approved. Approve-draft is the GUI face of the MT-081 activate transition.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New native pane src/frontend/handshake_native/src/role_manager_pane.rs registered in the native shell navigation; role-picker seam edits in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/operator_chat_pane.rs; React read-only components (RolePicker list/pick) under app/src/components/swarm/ wired to the MT-081 IPC read commands (list_handshake_roles / get_handshake_role); AccessKit metadata on every new control; Argus screenshot evidence; UserManual same-change update.

DETAILED SPEC — native Role Manager pane:
- List view: table of roles (id, title, current version, status badge draft/active/retired, provenance operator/imported) with status filter; stable AccessKit ids per row (role-row-{id}).
- Detail view: read-only render of the selected version (overlay_prompt markdown preview, tool_policy allow/deny, model_profile, transport_bindings, provenance incl. source_ref for imports); version-history selector.
- Create/edit: form producing a DRAFT (create) or a NEW DRAFT VERSION (edit) via the MT-081 HTTP/store API; kebab-id validation inline; editing never mutates an existing version (registry immutability surfaces as 'editing creates v{N+1} draft' in the UI copy).
- Approve-draft: explicit button with confirm step; calls activate; shows the one-active-version consequence (demotes prior active) before confirm. Retire likewise explicit + confirmed.
- Import review affordance: imported drafts show their ImportReport summary (dropped sections, warnings) when available, so approval is informed.
- Role picker in operator_chat_pane launch flow: dropdown/combo listing ACTIVE roles only (plus 'No role'), selection carried into the launch request alongside the existing lane/model selection (OperatorChatLaunchRequest seam; actual injection is MT-082's engine, spawn wiring for child sessions is MT-086). Picker shows role id + version so the operator knows exactly what will be injected.
- React read-only surface: RolePicker component in app/src/components/swarm/ (pattern siblings: OperatorChat.tsx, SwarmControlRoom.tsx) listing active roles via IPC read commands; pick feeds the React launch flow's request payload. NO create/edit/approve from React — write surfaces are native-only this MT.
- Non-intrusion: pane renders inside the existing native shell; no popup windows, no focus stealing; all evidence capture headless via Argus.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read operator_chat_pane.rs to match the existing pane structure, state handling, and AccessKit conventions; read app/src/components/swarm/OperatorChat.tsx for the React launch-flow request shape.
2. Implement role_manager_pane.rs list view against GET /api/roles (via the native backend client used by sibling panes), with status filter + stable ids.
3. Implement detail + version-history view.
4. Implement create/edit draft forms with inline kebab-id validation and 'creates new draft version' messaging.
5. Implement approve-draft (activate) and retire flows with confirm steps and typed-error surfacing (409/422 from MT-081 rendered as operator-readable messages, not toasts that vanish).
6. Integrate the role picker into the operator_chat_pane launch flow; extend the launch request seam with optional role_id + role_version.
7. Implement the React RolePicker (list/pick) over the IPC read commands; wire into the swarm launch UI payload.
8. AccessKit pass: every new interactive control gets a stable accessibility id + label; keyboard navigable.
9. Argus evidence: drive the pane headlessly — list, open detail, create draft, approve draft, picker-shows-active-only — capturing screenshots per target; attach artifact paths to build evidence.
10. UserManual same-change update: role-manager entry (purpose, navigation path, lifecycle walkthrough incl. import-review-approve, failure modes: backend down, version conflict, approval demotes prior active).

acceptance_criteria: Native Role Manager pane lists roles with id, title, version, status badge, provenance, and a working status filter; rows carry stable AccessKit ids.
Detail view renders overlay_prompt preview, tool_policy, model_profile, transport_bindings, provenance (incl. import source_ref), and version history.
Create produces a draft; edit produces a new draft version; the UI cannot mutate an existing version (registry immutability respected and surfaced in UI copy).
Approve-draft calls the MT-081 activate transition behind an explicit confirm that names the demotion of any prior active version; retire likewise explicit + confirmed.
Operator chat launch flow shows a role picker listing ACTIVE roles only (plus no-role), displaying id + version; the selection lands in the launch request payload.
React RolePicker lists the same active roles via the IPC read commands and feeds the swarm launch payload; React has no role write path.
All new controls are AccessKit-labeled and keyboard navigable.
Argus evidence exists for every argus_target; no foreground window popping or focus stealing during automated runs.
In-product UserManual role-manager entry updated in the same change with a self-consistency check against the shipped controls.

implementation_notes: Native GUI is egui (verified: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/operator_chat_pane.rs); follow its pane/state conventions rather than inventing a new pattern.

React siblings verified in app/src/components/swarm/: OperatorChat.tsx, SwarmControlRoom.tsx, SwarmBoard.tsx, swarm_spawn_visual_harness.tsx — add RolePicker beside them and reuse the existing visual-harness pattern for the React test surface.
Draft approval is THE operator-authority moment for roles (esp. MT-084 imports); friction here is deliberate — confirm dialogs must state consequences, never one-click approve.
Argus per .GOV/roles_shared/docs/ARGUS_VISUAL_INSPECTION_PROTOCOL.md: unit tests alone cannot satisfy HBR-VIS rows; screenshots go to the external artifacts root, never into the repo worktree.
Quiet duty: automated GUI drives must be headless/non-intrusive (no focus stealing, no popup windows) per HBR-QUIET.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.behavior: role lifecycle operations driven from the GUI (create/edit/approve/retire) and role-carrying launch requests
hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: GUI drives MT-081 store mutations whose ledger events are the Tier-1 surface; internal_diagnostics/Palmistry not yet shipped in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1.

risk_if_missed: Roles have no operator surface: drafts (incl. imports) cannot be reviewed or approved, launches cannot pick roles, and the operator-authors/approves-models-consume contract collapses into API-only usage no operator will perform.

risks: RISK-1: One-click approval — an approve button without consequence-naming confirm lets an operator activate an unreviewed (possibly imported) prompt by misclick; injection then runs unvetted text.
RISK-2: Picker shows drafts/retired — launching with a non-active role either fails late (typed error after launch UX) or, worse, injects unapproved text if the backend guard is bypassed.
RISK-3: React write creep — the 'read-only' React surface grows a create/approve call, splitting role authority across two GUIs and bypassing the native confirm flow.
RISK-4: Stale list after mutation — approve/retire in the native pane not reflected in the picker/React list, so the operator launches with a role state that no longer exists.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): approve/retire behind explicit confirm dialogs naming consequences (prior-active demotion); Argus target captures the confirm state; no keyboard default-accept on the destructive action.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): picker queries status=active only (test-pinned); backend NotActive guard (MT-082) remains the hard gate — GUI filtering is defense-in-depth, asserted in tests.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): React tests assert only list/get IPC commands are invoked; no write IPC command for roles exists to call (MT-081 exposes read-only IPC).
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): list/picker refresh after every mutation round-trip; test drives approve then asserts picker reflects the new active version.

research_provenance.source: Inspected native GUI surface src/frontend/handshake_native/src/operator_chat_pane.rs (egui pane + launch flow) and React swarm components app/src/components/swarm/ (OperatorChat.tsx, SwarmControlRoom.tsx, visual harnesses) as integration patterns; MT-081 registry API + read-only IPC as the data plane; Argus protocol .GOV/roles_shared/docs/ARGUS_VISUAL_INSPECTION_PROTOCOL.md for visual evidence discipline; operator context: roles are operator-authored/approved, model-consumed.
corrections: Write surfaces (create/edit/approve/retire) are native-only; React is strictly read-only list/pick this MT.
Approve-draft is the operator-authority moment — deliberate confirm friction, informed by the MT-084 ImportReport for imported drafts.
Picker exposes only active roles; the backend NotActive guard stays the hard gate.
